desert_p19_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_001.text: The older woman disliked the clinic window because it faced a wall. She had expected town to offer a view in exchange for the indignity of arriving on a stretcher. Her niece put the onion basket on the low table and said the wall was holding up somebody's roof, which seemed an honourable occupation. Bao laughed when she came for the field-to-ward review. The resident clinician's fuller assessment treated the lower-leg injury as a suspected fracture requiring support, monitoring and later checks; the hip pain appeared consistent with bruising but still belonged in the follow-up.

desert_p19_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_002.text: No one promised a fast return to stone work. The patient wanted a different window. This request was easier to consider than a different leg. The niece's shoulder had a load-related strain that needed rest from the provoking tasks and a gradual plan reviewed by the clinic. Her aunt complained that this meant two people would be forbidden to move the same basket. The niece said the basket could enjoy independence. The young worker's finger had been cleaned and dressed under the fuller clinic review, with a scheduled recheck and clear instructions about work.

desert_p19_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_003.text: He asked whether he could still attend the school enquiry. The clinician allowed the ordinary counter visit after rest, keeping the hand protected, and forbade him to demonstrate smithing at the interview. He accepted the terms as though the course had already become slightly more real. Yue visited only after Bao and the patients agreed. She brought a small paper flower purchased from the town market, visibly different from the onion skins, and no unsolicited advice about how to be grateful. The older woman asked whether her brother's well had reopened. Yue had no news yet and said so.

desert_p19_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_004.text: The woman stared at the wall, then asked for the copy of her grandmother's receipt. Du's office had made a modern copy with its limits marked, the original still at home. Yue promised to ask him for it that afternoon. It was a small concrete errand. She liked being able to agree to something whose route she actually knew. At the municipal receiving house, the records clerk had found the transfer packet's catalogue entry. The packet itself occupied a closed shelf because its wrapper had suffered during an old roof leak.

desert_p19_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_005.text: Access required a staff handling appointment rather than Du taking it down immediately. The conservator had been asked to review it in her reading-house role the following morning. Du stood beside the counter with the expression of a man whose treasure had acquired another queue. His apprentice arrived carrying the paid correction account and two revised proofs. She informed him that neither would sign itself while he admired a catalogue. He followed her back to the office before she had to repeat it.

desert_p19_006.speaker: du_she
desert_p19_006.text: You have kept the first warning circulation moving while I was away. I should have left a better source note for the rival press's correction, and I should have told you the old letter was part of the enquiry. Here are the actual field copies and the receiving number. I want your name on the wrapper work and comparison you prepare, with the paid time recorded. I also want you to tell me which part of this bundle is impossible to read in the order I have given it to you. Do not spare me because I returned tired.

desert_p19_007.speaker: du_she
desert_p19_007.text: I have grown inconveniently talented at mistaking my fatigue for other people's obligation.

desert_p19_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_008.text: The apprentice examined the bundle and said the order was excellent if its reader already knew everything. Du winced. She put the route restriction first, the source chronology second, current observations third, and the old packet enquiry last. Then she added a list of still unanswered questions. Gao, arriving with the current level drawing, approved the structure and disputed one caption. The apprentice asked her to write the correction in the margin rather than stand explaining it above the desk. Gao obeyed.

desert_p19_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_009.text: Yue felt a private pleasure at seeing both senior professionals trained by the person who would have to make their work usable. The apprentice looked tired too, but no longer invisible. The municipal supply receipt arrived at Han's yard before noon. The dispatched service cart had reached Onion Hollow on the previous afternoon by the inspected high approach, keeping within its current permitted load. Its driver and the household keeper signed for two hundred clean litres actually received into the cisterns after distribution had made room. The carriage record showed no caravan return credit; the stock belonged to the community.

desert_p19_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_010.text: A receiving officer had begun reviewing the well closure and lining condition. The source remained closed. Gao read the actual delivery time twice, then made a brief public update. The request had become a delivered quantity, and its limits could be said without diminishing what it meant. The community's note thanked the party without treating the water as a deed. It also complained about the new cart-line warning being too long for the service driver to read quickly. Gao accepted both lines. The keeper wanted the load limit and turning instruction larger, while the conservation and ownership notes could follow.

desert_p19_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_011.text: Du's apprentice made the change on the next proof. Han read the note at his kitchen table while his daughter ate an apricot beside him. She said the keeper sounded like her grandmother. Han said every well probably needed somebody willing to be that annoying. His mother, within hearing, asked whether he would like his soup without water tonight. The crop claimant from the grass village came to the same office with the junction note. The reception room now held two different communities asking how northern water had been directed.

desert_p19_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_012.text: The clerk began to combine their claims under one heading, then stopped when the woman pointed to the separate district numbers. The grass field's damage and Onion Hollow's source closure required related evidence but different remedies. Gao stayed long enough to explain the shared diversion sequence. She charged the paid meeting time under the approved commission rather than invent another free day out of professional guilt. The woman said she preferred a surveyor who could return next week to one exhausted by being generous today.

desert_p19_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_013.text: At the cooperative's afternoon review, Han presented the water transfer, patient transport and stored-cargo costs together with their actual authorizations. The freight chair read the three hundred litres against the source closure and weight plan, then checked the two-day return stock. The protected compartments had stayed sealed on this trip; the previous trip's necessary five-litre draw remained honestly recorded in its own account. Nobody tried to use one result to erase the other. The rival publisher's representative asked whether the donation might be charged to his contribution.

desert_p19_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_014.text: The chair said it had come from the agreed common emergency provision, whose purpose he had signed before departure. He read his copy and subsided.

desert_p19_015.speaker: han_xun
desert_p19_015.text: The stored cargo is one hundred and thirty kilograms. We have its signed inventory and custody term, with a collection fee still to pay. I propose an ordinary collection wagon after the responsible route inspection confirms passage, not a third expedition dressed as an errand. The relay box remains partly unread and protected in place. A return conservation visit needs its own staff, weather window and funding. We can arrange both jobs separately. The emergency has not made them free, and it has not made Lin Yue their permanent owner.

desert_p19_016.speaker: han_xun
desert_p19_016.text: She has returned the field flags and is still entitled to have a day that belongs to her.

desert_p19_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_017.text: Yue looked up, startled to hear that last sentence in a payment review. Han had seen her carrying a bowl to the clinic and assumed she would soon be collecting another unpaid obligation. He was not entirely wrong. The chair asked whether she wanted to continue as an assistant if a funded return visit was approved. Yue said she would consider the exact work, but wanted the present hire closed first. Gao nodded beside her, perhaps hearing an answer she had needed to give at her own licensing office.

desert_p19_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_018.text: The clerk put Yue's name under completed field term rather than available indefinitely. The ink made the boundary pleasantly visible. The source officer's initial report reached the room late. Surface flow had approached an external lining junction and carried grit beneath one cover seating point. The shaft's deeper lining showed no immediate structural failure in the accessible inspection, but the draw required controlled flushing, source checks and a repaired cover arrangement before reopening. The officer would keep the closure while that work proceeded. The repair did not depend on pouring new wet masonry and declaring it cured by sunset.

desert_p19_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_019.text: Sound fitted components could restore the cover and splash barrier, after which the actual source condition still needed clearance. Bao read the proposed sequence and asked for the receiving clinic to see the source results before any seasonal treatment room used it. The younger valley representative's reply was attached. He still wanted irrigation for the lower garden, but now requested a reviewed seasonal branch rather than letting the new flow choose its own route. The woman who feared the water asked for the low path warning retained even after levels fell.

desert_p19_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_020.text: The well keeper asked for the spare rope again, attaching a price from the local supplier. Three distinct wants remained distinct on the page. The chair authorized the rope under source maintenance, with receipt required. Du smiled at that little victory. Yue hoped the keeper would enjoy being able to argue with a rope that was actually new. At dusk the young worker went to the metal school's enquiry counter with the municipal driver. Yue accompanied them as far as the lane, then left them their own meeting.

desert_p19_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_021.text: The new room was easy to find once the driver stopped following last term's sign. An admissions clerk gave the applicant a schedule, fee table and basic reading assessment date after his medical recheck. No place was promised on the strength of a rescue. The young man came out carrying the papers as if they were a tool he had not yet learned to use. He looked frightened and pleased. Yue recognised the combination from her first proper cultivation school day. His family could contribute part of the course fee.

desert_p19_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_022.text: The rest would require paid work within his recovered hand limits and perhaps the district's ordinary training grant, for which he had to apply. The municipal driver offered the public grant form he had obtained for his brother, not the brother's reserved funds. The two applicants could help each other understand the instructions later. The young worker wrote the grant deadline carefully on the wrapper. His finger prevented a neat last stroke, and he let it remain crooked. The course would begin next month.

desert_p19_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_023.text: His life had more in it now than the bridge that had broken, but the bridge had not bought him an instant future. The niece wanted to see the town workshop employing the women the driver mentioned. Bao allowed a short ordinary visit after the clinical review, with the painful arm supported and no practical demonstration. She returned talking faster than she had since the rescue. One woman there made fine latch pieces, another handled accounts and stock, both paid for actual work. The niece had expected a single grand craft called metalwork and found a room of different tasks.

desert_p19_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_024.text: Her aunt listened from the ward bed and asked which task had no heavy stone. The niece described the fine latch work. The aunt said a good latch would be useful on their store, then stopped herself before turning interest into an immediate chore. Du brought the modern receipt copy that evening. The older patient held it where the light fell without glare, noticing her grandmother's rough mark before the formal entry. She remembered the woman's hands more clearly than the year written beside them. Du explained the transfer packet appointment and what it might establish.

desert_p19_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_025.text: She asked whether he would give the family the same result if it showed no balance remaining. He said yes. She studied him, then returned the copy to the dry wrapper. Her niece said the grandmother would have wanted the well kept sound either way. The patient replied that her grandmother would also have wanted the office to stop losing the story of who paid for it.

desert_p19_026.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p19_026.text: I came to visit, not to tell you the road was almost worse. You have enough of the road in that leg. Bao says it is allowed to be a troublesome leg until the clinic has done its work, and I am choosing to believe her because mine became much easier when I stopped negotiating with it. I brought ginger, this time at the correct destination. Du managed the purchase badly for years, but he eventually learned.

desert_p19_027.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p19_027.text: There is hope for mapmakers and injured guides alike, though neither group should be encouraged to make speeches beside a patient who wants her supper.

desert_p19_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_028.text: The patient laughed and asked Tuo to put the ginger where the niece would not use all of it at once. The niece pretended offence. Tuo sat in the sound chair by the bed with her own foot comfortable on the floor for the short visit. The two older women compared bad chairs, clinic windows and relatives who repaired things without being asked. Yue listened while the ward light turned gold. For a little while the world contained no unread register or threatened well, only people with enough energy to be annoyed by furniture.

desert_p19_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_029.text: When Bao came for the next check, the visitors left without making the patient earn her rest through another farewell. The municipal records appointment took place the following morning. The conservator opened the damaged outer wrapper under the reading room's controlled handling arrangement. Inside, several packets were intact enough for supported examination. Du identified the relay's household transfer number on one, then stayed outside the handling space while staff recorded it. The packet had not been hidden in a conspiracy; it had been shelved under the receiving district's later designation after a roof leak complicated access.

desert_p19_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_030.text: That explanation did not excuse the years in which nobody asked. It did make the next step plain. Staff could now compare the old receipt, transferred balance and later settlement entries in their proper sequence. The entries showed household credits carried into a district account, with several later returns and one unresolved notation requiring comparison with a separate disbursement register. The older woman's family appeared under a historic household identifier, not a present claimant automatically entitled to the same name. Their receipt matched an earlier contribution. A later entry suggested partial return, leaving a remainder to investigate.

desert_p19_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_031.text: The records clerk prepared a factual extract for the family and the responsible district office, retaining the originals under public custody. Du could publish the source correction without publishing every household's balances. He would have to wait for the remaining comparison before pretending the family story had reached its last page. Gao had hoped the old grades would be in the same packet. They were not. The separate works transfer remained linked to the relay box and lower exchange register, both partly inaccessible for different reasons. She took the disappointment outside and bought a pear from the market.

desert_p19_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_032.text: Yue walked with her. Gao said one could spend a whole career following receiving numbers and still fail to measure the next channel properly. Yue asked whether that meant the current measurements should be abandoned. Gao said no, bit the pear and visibly disliked the clarity of her own answer. A professional could want an elegant closure and still do the work that had no patience for elegance. At the route office, a current repair crew report finally gave the party's emergency line its next condition.

desert_p19_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_033.text: With flow lower, responsible staff had inspected the upper support, restricted the route and scheduled removal or proper incorporation of the temporary materials after the wider repair. A light collection wagon could approach within the posted limits on the appointed day, with the current driver checking conditions again. Han booked the wagon and the local custodian's release appointment. The stored one hundred and thirty kilograms now had a funded way home. Yue heard the appointment and felt a knot loosen. It was not her unfinished journey waiting in a shed.

desert_p19_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_034.text: It was a shipment with a person paid to collect it. The source supply schedule was extended for the closure period. Subsequent deliveries would be counted against actual household draws and the cisterns' combined four-hundred-litre capacity, using smaller loads where free space required. The first two-hundred-litre receipt remained the only arrival the town could already verify. The responsible officer named the next dispatch and receiving keeper; the community would send the signed quantity back. Bao approved the provision as a practical bridge while clearance proceeded, without promising that every test would pass on the first day.

desert_p19_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_035.text: The household representatives accepted the schedule and retained their own right to complain if it did not arrive. Water had acquired a calendar people could hold offices to. Han's daughter came to the receiving yard with a new signboard design. The flower had grown smaller; the wheel had acquired four sensible spokes. She put reliable carriage beneath it, then asked her father whether that sounded too dull. He said dull was becoming one of the better things a cart could be. Gao suggested the word current somewhere near any published route statement.

desert_p19_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_036.text: The daughter said surveyors would ruin a signboard if allowed too much space. Han bought her a cake and kept her design intact. Yue watched the family bicker comfortably, happy that the road had brought him a way to stay home without making home another failure of ambition. Bao went to the grass village keeper's town contact to discuss the possible seasonal treatment room. The room had a roof, but she still required its water provision, clean storage, privacy and actual transfer route examined.

desert_p19_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_037.text: She proposed a limited autumn term with paid staffing days and a referral agreement with the municipal clinic. The keeper asked what would happen when she was on field work. She said the room would close on posted dates unless another qualified person was contracted. He respected that more than an every-day sign she could not staff. The proposal went to the clinic board with a real budget and opening conditions. Kind interest had begun becoming a service someone could actually use.

desert_p19_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_038.text: Yue spent the afternoon washing the issued cloak one last time and returning it dry to Han's gear shelf. The receiving clerk checked the repair seam, accepted its ordinary wear and closed the loan term. The salt hat and light flag bag had already been returned; Gao's instrument glass remained hers by commission custody, not Yue's souvenir. Yue carried her habitual pack back through the market with room inside it. A seller offered a brass compass box that might or might not contain a useful compass. She admired it, asked the price and left it on the cloth.

desert_p19_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_039.text: Owning every interesting tool was not necessary to remember having learned beside one. At the rented room, the shopkeeper's daughter wanted to know whether the old lady was improving. Yue said the clinic was monitoring the injury and expected a longer recovery, with comfort better now that she was properly supported. The girl frowned at the lack of a triumphant answer. Then she asked whether anyone could visit without bringing flowers. Yue said a short approved visit and ordinary conversation might be welcome. The girl chose a story about the neighbour's cat stealing a dumpling.

desert_p19_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_040.text: It had no medical value, which was part of its appeal. She rehearsed the funniest section while Yue repaired her own notebook wrapper, finally laughing at a town disaster that ended before anybody needed a stretcher. The well keeper's next note arrived through the scheduled receiving wagon. The source remained closed, the replacement cover pieces had been fitted, and the officer's controlled clearance process continued. He acknowledged the spare rope actually received and the smaller clean delivery actually counted into available capacity. He also reported the sleeping-jars term had made the village children rename both cisterns.

desert_p19_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_041.text: Gao copied the useful facts and let Du keep the joke. The community had not waited passively for visitors to restore its world. It had counted, repaired, complained, stored and sent messages. In town, those verbs finally began to occupy as much space as the closed relay office's elegant old line. That evening Yue wrote a page about the well court without including a single grand discovery. Two cistern handles, a crooked willow, a service board's repaired corner, a rope high above a closed shaft. The page did not contain the keeper's private family balances or the patient's clinical details.

desert_p19_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_042.text: Those belonged in other places, under other care. She added the actual three hundred litres and the later municipal delivery, because those quantities explained why people could remain while work continued. Then she drew the tiny flower now beside the shoemaker's fish stone. The village had kept its well by treating a closure as work to do, not a verdict that it had ceased to be a village. The collection wagon left on the appointed morning with a contracted driver, two animals and its own measured travel stock. Han did not add its water to the returned expedition's account.

desert_p19_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_043.text: This was a different job, financed from the equipment recovery provision and documented under the route office's current conditions. The dry shed custodian had received the arrival date through the same scheduled carrier used for the source notes. Yue helped Han check the package list, then watched the wagon turn toward the Black Gate without feeling obliged to follow. Being useful at a departure table could be the whole task. The road did not require every person who had once walked it to keep walking. At the ward, the older patient had gained a view.

desert_p19_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_044.text: The new bed faced a narrow strip of sky between roofs, which she declared adequate compensation for another day's supported leg. Her niece had made an arrangement to stay in the town receiving house near the clinic, with its actual daily charge and a district transport allowance covering the initial emergency period. Longer accommodation still needed a decision. The niece refused Yue's offer to solve it from her wages. She wanted the family contact and responsible office to discuss it properly. Yue accepted the refusal without making it a test of gratitude. She could carry the message instead.

desert_p19_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_045.text: The patient's adult daughter arrived that afternoon from her ordinary town employment, having received the clinic's actual household contact message. She wore a flour-dusted sleeve and apologized for not coming sooner. Her mother said flour took priority over visitors, then held her hand tightly enough to contradict herself. Bao gave them the follow-up plan in a private conversation they both understood. The daughter could assist with meals and visits, but her rented room had a steep stair unsuitable for the supported leg. The clinic social clerk added that fact to the temporary accommodation enquiry.

desert_p19_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_046.text: A family existed; that did not make every room the family possessed fit for care. The niece feared the daughter would send her straight home to the wall work. Instead the daughter asked whether she could keep the patient company for a few days while her own shifts continued. The niece agreed on the condition that her shoulder receive the rest prescribed, not a different set of lifting chores in town. They made that agreement with Bao present and wrote the practical tasks down. The older woman complained that her relatives had become a committee.

desert_p19_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_047.text: Her daughter said committees would be a novelty for a woman who usually issued all instructions herself. The patient laughed, then asked them to keep talking where she could hear. Du's apprentice found the partial settlement reference in a neighbouring disbursement register during her paid comparison hours. It did not pay out the whole earlier contribution in cash; part had been returned as source maintenance labour credited to the district, and a later notation remained unclosed. The old account's units needed conversion before anyone named a modern amount. She brought the sequence to Du and the records clerk together.

desert_p19_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_048.text: Du asked whether the family should be told immediately. The clerk prepared a clear interim extract showing what was found and what still required review. A complex truth did not need to wait in silence merely because its final total was not yet ready.

desert_p19_049.speaker: du_she
desert_p19_049.text: The receipt's contribution was not just money dropped into a box. It was a share in keeping the well court working, partly settled in labour and partly transferred. I had reduced it to an old district credit because that fit a clean summary. The remaining notation belongs in the review, but nobody should sell the family a present water entitlement from an unfinished conversion. I will tell them the exact sequence and its limits. Then I will correct the public account of how the source was maintained.

desert_p19_050.speaker: du_she
desert_p19_050.text: That correction is due even if the later review finds no money left to return.

desert_p19_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_051.text: The older patient took the interim extract seriously, but not greedily. She asked whether the labour credited to the district had actually been performed at the well. The register referred to a lining season and household work, matching the community's old service board. The surviving entries supported that account, though the work's whole quality could not be recovered from paper. She pointed to her grandmother's mark and said the woman had always disliked seeing a good day's work become somebody else's generosity. The daughter listened beside her.

desert_p19_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_052.text: They agreed to submit a formal review request through the household representative, using the extract rather than a rumour that a buried box had made them rich. Gao carried the corrected source history to the licensing office with her supplemental field report. The clerk accepted the measured observations and the explicit limitations, then asked why the old grades remained unresolved. Gao said the site had been interrupted by a rising channel and medical evacuation. The condition record and copied transfer entries were attached. The clerk looked disappointed by the absence of a neat final grade.

desert_p19_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_053.text: She could feel her own disappointment reflected back at her. Then the reviewing surveyor signed the present warning and approved the independent field method within its scope. Her professional standing had not required a ruin to give up every answer on the first paid visit.

desert_p19_054.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p19_054.text: I thought they would hear interrupted and read failed. The reviewing surveyor heard the actual reason and asked whether I had preserved enough for another person to resume. I had. That is a much more useful question than the one I kept rehearsing in my head. I still want the drainage grades. I am not suddenly above wanting a beautiful complete result. But I can go back for them under a new scope, with the conservator and mason paid, or leave them for a better-prepared crew. My licence survives the difference.

desert_p19_055.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p19_055.text: I should have learned that before the valley taught it so loudly.

desert_p19_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_056.text: Yue took the news to Tuo, who had begun a longer local walk under her recovery plan. The guide reached the tea stall without a hitch in her stride and deliberately sat before pride could add another street. She said Gao had always expected examiners to see the worst version of her work first. Gao said Tuo had always expected guides to be judged by how much pain they concealed. They looked at one another, then laughed with considerable irritation. Yue ordered the ordinary tea before either could improve the argument into a philosophy.

desert_p19_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_057.text: The owner recognized them and brought the same pot without offering four unnecessary varieties. A boy at the stall asked Tuo whether she had met the cultivator's snake. She pointed at Yue's ordinary pack and said it was still a lead, unfortunately. He had brought a wooden toy snake to show her, painted with black bands. Yue admired the moving joints and kept it away from the packed practice lead. The boy explained how a local carpenter made the sections turn. Gao examined the joint with professional interest and asked what the toy weighed.

desert_p19_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_058.text: He had no idea, and thought her question peculiar. For once a surveyor let a thing remain unmeasured. She gave it back before curiosity could become a new commission. Bao's seasonal-room proposal passed its first review with conditions. The existing shed required a cleanable work surface, screened storage, a maintained water arrangement and a written transfer link to the municipal clinic. The clinic board approved a limited autumn pilot after inspection and preparation, funded jointly by the village's service contribution and a route-health allocation. It would open on posted staffed days, not pretend to be a permanent emergency ward.

desert_p19_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_059.text: Bao read the approval at Han's receiving bench and looked more frightened than pleased. Yue asked why. Bao said a possible room could be blamed on circumstances; an approved room would require her to show up and do the work.

desert_p19_060.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p19_060.text: I wanted this enough to keep talking about it on the road. Now the board has given it a narrow real shape and I find myself missing the comforting size of a wish. The first staffed days will be after the preparations and source arrangements pass, not tomorrow. I have to train an attendant in the ordinary cleaning and receiving tasks, without letting anyone call that medical qualification. I have to make the referral schedule work. It is possible. That is the frightening part.

desert_p19_061.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p19_061.text: If you hear me wishing for another expedition just to postpone the opening, remind me that the valley has already given me enough reasons to begin.

desert_p19_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_062.text: The collection wagon returned with all one hundred and thirty kilograms of listed inspection cargo accounted for, measured within ordinary handling tolerance and checked package by package. The local custodian's release receipt named the actual date and storage fee. The driver had followed the current restricted route notice, found the temporary works unchanged at the receiving check and kept within the permitted load. Han paid the remaining custody and carriage charges from the designated provision. The materials used in the emergency support remained under the route authority's separate inspection record. Yue helped return the long boards to their hired rack.

desert_p19_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_063.text: The dry shed had become somebody else's ordinary shed again. The driver brought the well keeper's latest source note too. The fitted cover and splash barrier had passed the structural inspection, while flushing and source clearance still continued. A smaller supply load had been received within the free cistern capacity, not poured into an imaginary reservoir because the district wanted a round number. The keeper recorded the household draws against each vessel separately. He also sent an onion-skin flower tied around the new rope invoice. Han's daughter took it off before filing the receipt, then asked permission to keep it.

desert_p19_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_064.text: The flower had no custody restriction and no balance attached. Han said yes and watched her pin it beside the signboard sketch. The route authority proposed a properly funded return conservation visit after the source and access inspections allowed it. This time the purpose would be the unread relay material and drainage sequence, with the actual household interests represented. Gao and the conservator would prepare the scope; the mason would reassess access; the district would supply custody authority and transport. The field budget included staff pay, clean travelling water, animal provision, return margin and a weather delay allowance.

desert_p19_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_065.text: No person had yet been ordered to leave on an unfunded date. Du offered a contribution and accepted that the schedule would be set by those conditions rather than his appetite for the box. The rival publisher wanted equal access to the eventual public findings, not private ownership of the fragment. He signed the same release terms and asked whether a drawing of the room could accompany the correction. Gao agreed to a measured exterior and permitted interior-position view, making the unsafe areas visible rather than cropping them for drama.

desert_p19_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_066.text: Yue heard the man describe the picture as less attractive than his original palace-like cover. Du said it would sell fewer fantasies and perhaps more useful sheets. The representative replied that useful sheets also needed buyers. Nobody disproved him. They arranged a modest paid print run instead of pretending truth made paper and ink free. The niece visited the latch makers again on an approved short walk and asked about entry work that did not load the healing shoulder.

desert_p19_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_067.text: One offered paid sorting and simple marking tasks for a few hours after the clinician cleared that level, with no promise of a full apprenticeship. She would need accuracy and attendance. The niece accepted the information, then returned to the ward instead of beginning immediately. Her aunt wanted to know why she looked pleased. She said she had found a room where people might eventually pay her to notice small things. The older woman considered this and said small things had been ruining large things for years; perhaps it was a useful trade.

desert_p19_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_068.text: The young worker's course enquiry became a grant application with help from the ordinary public counter. His household contribution and proposed light paid work were listed, his recovery review date attached. The municipal driver's brother applied separately. They would sit the same basic assessment if both remained eligible. Yue lent the worker no certificate and recommended no special waiver. She helped him copy one difficult character into the correct box because he asked. When he finished, he folded the form carefully around the deadline slip. His bandaged finger looked awkward against the neat paper.

desert_p19_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_069.text: The future had not ceased being uncertain, but uncertainty now came with a date and a door he could find. At the clinic, the older patient was sleeping when her daughter brought a small mirror. The niece put it where the woman could see the strip of sky and part of the courtyard from bed. On waking, she declared the arrangement far superior to moving the wall. Bao checked her supported leg, recorded the ongoing findings and confirmed the next review. The household still needed suitable temporary lodging after the ward no longer supplied the right kind of care.

desert_p19_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_070.text: The social clerk was looking at accessible rooms near the clinic. The patient listened without pretending she could climb her daughter's steep stair. She had stopped offering her injured body as a solution to other people's rent. Yue returned to the practice room for a quiet paid session only after proper sleep and ordinary recovery. The guarded receiving station and familiar lead gave her the same bounded stage-five task, with the same ceiling and independent stop.

desert_p19_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_071.text: She made no new admission trial, claimed no greater reserve and left the station before another repetition could become a way to avoid her thoughts. Outside, the town sounded unusually full: wheels, vendors, a school bell, a basin poured into a garden. Her trained routes belonged to her body, earned and limited. The road had given her knowledge beyond them without making every new knowledge a higher stage. The keeper's last note of that week contained a sentence Gao copied at the top of the community update: the well remained theirs while it was closed.

desert_p19_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p19_072.text: It was a statement about responsibility and use, not an invented private deed. The households had maintained the source, received measured temporary supply, repaired the cover and sought clearance. Neither the district number nor a publisher's summary could make that work disappear. Yue read the sentence at the receiving bench while Han's daughter pinned the flower beside the wheel design. Beyond town, light would be touching the relay floor again. In the hollow, people were still keeping count because they intended to keep living there.
